name: cp2k
desc: Quantum chemistry and solid state physics software package
why: Real quantum chemistry and solid-state simulation you can run at home, though it is heavy and specialised.

brief.what_it_is: CP2K is a quantum chemistry and solid state physics software package for atomistic simulation of solid, liquid, molecular, periodic, material, crystal and biological systems. Its main method is DFT using the mixed Gaussian and plane waves approaches GPW and GAPW, and it also supports MP2, RPA, GW, tight-binding (xTB, DFTB), semi-empirical methods (AM1, PM3, PM6, RM1, MNDO) and classical force fields (AMBER, CHARMM). You feed it an input file describing the system and the calculation, and it runs molecular dynamics, metadynamics, Monte Carlo, Ehrenfest dynamics, vibrational analysis, core level spectroscopy, energy minimization, and NEB or dimer transition state searches. The README does not spell out the exact output format beyond a REFERENCES section in the output.
brief.why_it_exists: The project is presented as a general framework for many atomistic modelling methods in one code, with the stated aim that it is free and open so people can try it and modify it as needed. The homepage says it is available under the GPL and comes without warranty or direct support.
brief.how_it_works: CP2K is written in Fortran 2008 and runs in parallel using a mix of multi-threading, MPI and GPU acceleration (CUDA for NVIDIA, HIP/ROCm for AMD, and OpenCL). The README names Quickstep, FIST and QM/MM as key parts of the code, and says the source is organised into src, data (basis sets and pseudopotentials), docs, tests, tools and benchmarks directories.

commands_seen.context: Clones the current development master branch of the source code into a folder called cp2k; the README says this is the preferred route for developers.
Template for cloning a numbered release branch (replace x.y with the version, e.g. support/v2025.1); --recursive pulls in submodules.

brief.install_notes: The README points to the CP2K manual's installation pages with three routes: build from source, build with Spack, or install from a distribution package. End users are told to download a versioned tarball (cp2k-X.Y.tar.bz2) from the GitHub Releases page; developers are told to fork and git clone. Package badges in the README show availability via Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu, Homebrew, Docker (cp2k/cp2k), Spack and conda-forge. Source builds need the dependency setup described in the manual, which I did not read. The Homebrew metadata lists executables including cp2k.psmp and cp2k.popt (MPI and OpenMP-hybrid builds per the naming), plus several unit-test and miniapp binaries; that list came from the package metadata, not the README.
brief.standout: It is one code that covers DFT, wavefunction methods, semi-empirical and classical force field work in one input-file-driven package, which is unusual. The Fortran 2008 codebase is also developed in the open on GitHub, and the README points to a public test dashboard for architectures.
brief.status: Maintained, based on the README and homepage: the homepage says active development happens on GitHub, the README links a release badge, a dashboard of tested architectures and packaging across many distributions, and the wiki page was last modified 2026/04/10. I did not see a release date or latest commit date, so treat this as likely current rather than confirmed.
brief.caveats: No warranty and no direct support, according to the homepage. The homepage calls it 'heavy and specialised' only in the scout notes, not in the project's own text, and the README does not say it runs on a laptop; it needs real compute for most systems, and its installs need compilers and MPI-style setup for parallel use. The README does not describe a graphical interface; work is driven by input files, and it expects users to understand the underlying theory. The licence is GPL per the homepage.
quotes: CP2K is a quantum chemistry and solid state physics software package that can perform atomistic simulations of solid state, liquid, molecular, periodic, material, crystal, and biological systems.
CP2K is written in Fortran 2008 and can be run efficiently in parallel using a combination of multi-threading, MPI, and GPU acceleration
Please note that CP2K comes without any warranty or direct support.
